## Body

#221 correctness review, round 1: PASS-WITH-NOTES

Exact head: `e6a8c4a2cac6f9494fb273d03dbcb88c96f00233`. No blocking correctness finding.

The send resolves `role:prime` exclusively from the requested project's `prime_id`, ignoring open and released prime assignments and skipping the ordinary seat-role mismatch check for this designation (`crates/daemon/src/delivery/role_send.rs:242-262,355-361,379-409`). No designation produces no prime candidate, never a fallback to a legacy row; absent/tombstoned designated seats fail the existing live-seat check and queue. Routes uses the same project designation and filters out every prime assignment (`http/routes.rs:78-102`). `directory assign prime` remains refused under C24, so an assignment cannot redirect the queue through normal assignment draining.

**N001, nonblocking: routes does not show the designated holder's availability.** The new routes branch appends `prime_id` without checking the registry, unlike send. A missing/tombstoned designated seat therefore still appears by name under “Holder now” while role sends queue. Keep the designation as the sole identity source, but omit or annotate an unavailable holder, or document this display limitation. This does not redirect delivery to another seat.

The stated existing-queue limitation is accurate: designation does not drain already queued requests, and replay preserves existing request identity rather than sending it again.
